gloss: to bring someone/something home; to take back with one

definitions.gloss: to bring someone home; to take someone back
definitions.explanation: To bring a person or animal back to one's home or starting point. Implies accompaniment — the speaker goes together with the person or creature being brought.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}る。
{迷|まよ}い{猫|ねこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I ended up bringing a stray cat home.

examples.japanese: {友|とも}だち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{酔|よ}っ{払|ぱら}った⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦タクシー→タクシー：00816_takushii⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: My friend got drunk, so I took them home by taxi.

notes:
A compound verb expression combining ⟦{連|つ}れる→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧ (to take along, to bring a person) in its て-form with ⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧ (to return home). The subject accompanies the object back — it cannot be used for sending someone home alone.

USAGE:
Conjugates via the ⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧ portion (godan verb): {連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}らない, {連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}った, {連|つ}れて{帰|かえ}ろう, etc.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{連|つ}れて→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to take someone along (going away from home)
- ⟦{連|つ}れて→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧: to bring someone here
- {送|おく}り{届|とど}ける: to escort/deliver someone — more formal, implies responsibility
- {連|つ}れ{戻|もど}す: to bring back — stronger nuance of retrieval or compulsion
